analysis: Examined base text of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 1-797) and the head patch adding lines 595-611, which document a Gated DeltaNet prefill kernel selection for qwen3_5, qwen3_5_moe and prism_hadamard_qwen35. Behavior: per-process, per-instantiation probe tries packed then rows kernels on a fixed probe window, keeps the first that is bit-identical to gated_delta_step on GPU, else the stock kernel. Decode/MTP/masked/short windows use the stock kernel. DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED is an operator A/B override that can force packed or rows. This is documentation-only; no source is in this batch. Security relevance: T-041 checkpoint/prefix reuse relies on recurrent-state equivalence; the doc claims bit-exact selection preserves that. Forced packed/rows via env bypasses the bit-exact probe, which could make captured checkpoints differ from cold prefill, but this is an operator-controlled local setting (ADV-001 already controls the machine; T-007/T-012 output-integrity concerns pre-exist) and affects correctness, not cross-tenant confidentiality; cache scoping (cacheSalt) is unchanged. The fixed probe window is not consumer-derived, so no consumer-controlled input reaches selection per the doc. No authorization, attestation, encryption, billing or data-exposure changes are described. Integration question: verify in GatedDelta.swift/configuration.md that forced kernels are not default and that probe failures (MLX faults) are caught rather than crashing (availability, T-029-like), and whether forced non-bit-exact kernels can publish prefix checkpoints reused by later requests.
